items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: after we had made this recording, Randy Hall took the job. He's a very good band to play. He's like me. He studied violin. And he got to be a professor. He's out in California somewhere.

ctx.x: How long did you stay in Pensacola?

Oh, I think it was, let's see, I went there in 24, I must have came around about, no, about 20 years, about three years, about 27 years. I said, well, when the job was closed and we left Pensacola, and one stayed in Mobile, and they had a union there. They had a union in Jacksonville. We didn't have no union, black union in New Orleans. And when I was coming back, I told my daddy, this thing was really getting bad. And I, people always taught me, always had something to say, you know. I wrote and told my daddy, I…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: Well, Randy and I was good friends

ctx.x: You never did join the WPA band then?

No, I was going to say, I always thought that was a little too slow money for me. I, I, well I should have because there wasn't nothing to it, you know. Most of the guys got in just for the money of it, you see. But like I say, then I was doing a little range, I was selling arrangements around you and everything, you know. But I, I, in other words, I was doing it just as good as those guys there, you see. So, and then another thing I, I didn't like it because the time that, like, you would get a good job, it…
